A22.notes: Re-verified on the S6 final tree — the full suite re-ran green and the refs above now point at the S6 JUnit (same specs, both engines); the measurements quoted below are the historical ones from the slice that delivered this ID, and the S6 re-run numbers are in docs/evidence/S6/e2e.log. Headless-Linux numbers only. The DEFAULT pipeline (deterministic rules cleanup) meets every budget: OCR stage <= 5 s per fixture on the whole clean set in BOTH engines (RED-run chromium numbers: 2380 ms cold incl. worker boot, 286-898 ms warm; the green run's numbers are in e2e.log) and on the 4000 px huge01 fixture (~0.6-2 s); the default cleanup is 0-4 ms in-browser (postclip:cleanup measure) and mean ~0.5 ms / max far under 60 s over ALL 40 fixtures' gold inputs host-side. Memory: peak usedJSHeapSize 10 MiB across the clean-set eval in headless Chromium (performance.memory); this WebKit build exposes no performance.memory, so WebKit memory numbers are NOT_RUN (an engine limitation, recorded — not skipped silently). The OPT-IN LLM cleanup path is NOT asserted against the 60 s budget and never was: it ships DISABLED BY DEFAULT (the S4/A19 measured decision) and its real numbers on this tree are re-measured by eval_llm_vs_baseline (65-236 s single-threaded WASM, fail-closed cap 240 s) and recorded in the S5 e2e.log + limitations — exceeding the budget by design of that decision, disclosed, not hidden.

A28.notes: Re-verified on the S6 final tree — the full suite re-ran green and the refs above now point at the S6 JUnit (same specs, both engines); the measurements quoted below are the historical ones from the slice that delivered this ID, and the S6 re-run numbers are in docs/evidence/S6/e2e.log. Memory safety for large inputs, both engines: the 4000 px committed fixture (huge01) and a ~20 MB generated image (19.9 MB, 3200x1900, deterministic seeded noise + a readable text band, generated at run time by scripts/gen_large_fixture.mjs and NEVER committed — committed fixtures stay under the plan's size caps) are each processed with no crash, no hang (bounded by the spec's 240 s hang bound), no tab failure, zero page errors, the tab still evaluates afterwards, and a normal pick works right after. huge01 reaches review with its gold body text; the adversarial-noise input reaches a DESIGNED terminal state — review text where the OCR output carries enough English (measured: Chromium), or the English gate's fail-closed rejection of non-English-looking garbage (measured: this WebKit build lands there; UC10/UC11's designed behavior for unreadable input — never a crash, never a hang, never a silent empty screen). Stage timings + heap are recorded per engine in e2e.log (chromium RED numbers: decode 1132 ms, downscale 697 ms, OCR 29,756 ms, cleanup 2 ms, heap 10 MiB). DISCLOSED LIMITATION (not a hidden miss): the ~20 MB ADVERSARIAL-NOISE stress input's OCR stage (~30 s chromium / ~45-50 s webkit) exceeds the 5 s per-fixture OCR budget of A22; the RED run captured that failure honestly (red.log), two mitigations were measured and rejected (tesseract PSM SINGLE_BLOCK for downscaled inputs: no effect, 29.7 s vs 30.1 s — the cost is the LSTM pass over noise glyphs; lowering the 2600 px OCR cap further would trade away real large screenshots' legibility), and A28's own criterion — crash/hang/tab-failure-free processing — is what the eval asserts, per the plan's acceptance table. Every PLAN fixture stays within the A22 budget.

A29.notes: Re-verified on the S6 final tree — the full suite re-ran green and the refs above now point at the S6 JUnit (same specs, both engines); the measurements quoted below are the historical ones from the slice that delivered this ID, and the S6 re-run numbers are in docs/evidence/S6/e2e.log. The PRODUCTION build (npm run build, served from dist/ by vite preview) is proven clean in BOTH engines. (1) BUNDLE INSPECTION (scripts/inspect_bundle.mjs, committed output docs/evidence/S5/bundle-inspection.txt): zero occurrences of every test-hook marker (__postclipLlmDebug, testModelUrl, testProbe, parseTestFlags, __POSTCLIP_TEST_BUILD__), no eval/new Function in the app's own bundles, no source maps, all index.html resources same-origin, and the strict CSP meta VERBATIM. The NEGATIVE CONTROL (bundle-inspection-test-build.txt) runs the same detector against the TEST build and TRIPS on 4 hook occurrences — proving the detector detects. CI re-runs the live check after every production build (scripts/test.sh). (2) BEHAVIORAL: the ?testModelUrl/?testProbe query flags are INERT in production (the model card stays in its real probed state, no unsupported banner) and window.__postclipLlmDebug is never created; the smoke flow (pick -> real OCR -> review -> share spy + real clipboard) passes served from dist/ with zero console errors. (3) THE STRICT CSP SHIPS AND IS ENFORCED: default-src 'none'; script-src/style-src/img-src/manifest-src/worker-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' + THE PINNED MODEL HOST ONLY (https://huggingface.co); base-uri/form-action/object-src 'none'; no unsafe-eval, no unsafe-inline (inline scripts are BLOCKED — asserted through the engine's own CSP-violation signal in both engines); the app's own legitimate loads all work under it (same-origin workers incl. the OCR worker, the SW registration + precache, the OCR assets, the manifest). The TEST build's CSP differs by exactly one connect-src origin (the local model server http://127.0.0.1:4599) — asserted by inspection on both builds. frame-ancestors is deliberately absent from the meta policy: the CSP spec ignores it in meta; it belongs to the hosting layer (plan D10 keeps hosting out of scope).

A30.notes: Real-phone LLM speed/RAM and WebGPU behavior are the plan's D12 OPTIONAL device pass; no real phone is attached to this runner, so nothing was run and nothing is claimed. On this Linux host WebGPU is NOT_RUN by plan decision D8 (headless Chromium exposes navigator.gpu backed by a software adapter; WebKit does not expose it) — no WebGPU-path claim is made anywhere in the app or docs. The headless-Linux reality is measured and disclosed instead: the single-threaded WASM path runs the pinned 0.6B at ~2.3 tokens/s (65-240 s per cleanup; the S6 final-tree re-run measured 112-240 s with several fixtures hitting the 240 s fail-closed cap — recorded in e2e.log and docs/evidence/S4/llm-eval-chromium.json), the LLM ships disabled by default (A19), and WebKit-on-Linux cannot load the 397 MB model at all (engine measurement, S4) — the app falls back loudly. Real-device numbers would come from the owner's optional pass; the checklist is in docs/evidence/S6/conformance_report.md.
